races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
races.verdict: Not a strong maiden and it would be no surprise to see BOLD COMMANDER leave behind a couple of lesser efforts and get off the mark now fitted with blinkers. Sonny Hayes is an interesting newcomer, while Sapphire Sun could do better if settling down.

runners.note: 155,000 gns foal, 300,000 gns yearling, Blackbeard colt. Half-brother to several winners, including smart 5f/6f winner Beckford. Looked very green behind Folsom Blues on debut at Gowran (7f, 10/3) in June. Inexperienced

Fifth in strong 6f maiden at the Curragh on debut, and although he hasn't progressed, this looks an ordinary contest and he's certainly one of the main contenders if first-time blinkers have the desired effect.
Made more impact than previously when held in third in 6f maiden here 3 weeks ago, not knocked about having again taken a keen hold. Needs another step forward.
Yard knows this family well but he showed only greenness in 6f Naas maiden on debut a fortnight ago and will probably need more time.
Probably needed the run on debut at the Curragh (6f) 6 weeks ago and should last longer this time. Cheekpieces go on.
Foaled March 19. 175,000 gns foal, Blue Point colt. Dam unraced half-sister to useful 2-y-o 6f winner Nidhaal. Makes plenty of appeal on paper starting out in a thin maiden.

Made an encouraging start when running on late to fill second spot in a Down Royal maiden (5f) at the start of the month. May have found next race at Dundalk coming too soon just a fortnight on and faces a similar turnar

€250,000 No Nay Never filly. Half-sister to several winners, including very smart 1m-1¼m winner Prague. Little impact in 6f Naas maidens and looks one for handicaps over further next year. Tongue tie goes on.
Hasn't beaten another rival in 2 Naas maidens.
No show in 5f maidens.
Foaled April 21. Kuroshio filly. Dam maiden half-sister to smart winner up to 9f Lush Lips.
Shaped well on debut at Naas but proved much too headstrong in Curragh sales race a fortnight ago. Drops to 5f and could still do better.
Showed a bit more than on debut when mid-field at Down Royal and looks one for handicaps.

races.name: JDL Consultants Ltd Apprentice Handicap
races.verdict: DECALOGUE was value for a good deal extra when off the mark at Kempton 2 weeks ago so a 3 lb rise may not be enough to prevent the follow up. Oman is now 2 lb lower than for his Goodwood win in June when refitted in this headgear, so is next best ahead of Pangbourne.

runners.note: Registered a fourth career success when scoring at Nottingham on return and held her form well since, doing best of the older horses at Goodwood last time.
Hasn't shown his form on turf in 7 attempts since August 2023 and others are much preferred.
Winless since June last year when she completed a 5-timer. Underwhelming this season and first-time headgear needs to have a positive effect.
Strong-travelling maiden who looked a shade unfortunate at Doncaster in June. Reportedly finished lame at Ayr since.
Three-time winner in France. Made a bright start over hurdles for this yard last spring but best watched after 16 months off.

Low-mileage 3-y-o who is steadily improving in handicaps and did very well to open his account at Kempton in this headgear 2 weeks ago, motoring home from a moderate position. Promises to stay this far and 3 lb rise look
Winner at Goodwood in June when refitted with this headgear. Just respectable efforts at best since but he's now dipped below his last winning mark.

Confirmed the promise he had shown at 2 yrs when making a winning return in Lingfield novice in February. However, he hasn't managed to find any improvement in handicaps subsequently and headgear now applied.
Produced a career best under a well-judged ride when making all at Haydock this time last year. Likely to have needed belated return at Kempton 7 weeks ago and she won second time up last season.
Cheap purchase but has fared a bit better with each start in all-weather maidens. Up in trip for handicap bow.

Ended 2025 on a low-key note but caused a surprise after 10 months off when shedding her maiden tag at Salisbury. Only just denied the follow up at Brighton next time but went back to going lethargically in first-time he
Showed promise on all-weather earlier this year and hasn't fared at all badly switched to turf subsequently, another good third at Sandown latest.

races.name: Christmas Party Day Dancing At Ayr Racecourse Apprentice Handicap
races.verdict: Sole 3-y-o LEOPARDS ROCK can trump his much more exposed rivals with a return to further likely to bring more improvement. Empirestateofmind was only just denied the follow up at Hamilton 9 days ago so is feared most ahead of Arkenstaar, who arrives fresh after a light campaign.

runners.note: Runner-up on his first 3 runs at 1m this season. Failed to beat a rival next 2 starts but took a step back in the right direction when fourth at Carlisle 3 weeks ago.

Veteran who won twice last season, including off a much higher mark, and cashed in on drop in grade over C&D earlier this month. Only just denied at Hamilton 2 days later and must be considered in current mood.

Front runner who enhanced a good course record when scoring over C&D in July. Justified support when resuming winning ways at Musselburgh the following month but well below par both starts since and still yet to convince

Thrived last autumn when a 3-time 1m winner. Ran well when third at Hamilton on return in May but below par both starts since, though shaping as if needing Carlisle run 3 weeks ago after 4 months off. Has now dipped belo
Back down in class but she's a customary slow starter who has yet to threaten this season, remote third at Chester latest.

Similar form first 4 starts but showed some improvement on his second start in a handicap when fourth at Carlisle 3 weeks ago, shaping as if a return to this trip will suit. By far the least exposed here (sole 3-y-o).
Quirky maiden who has been firmly knocking on the door in recent weeks. Shaped as if still in form at Hamilton last time (made a big early move) and expected to be competitive again.
Three-time C&D winner who was ridden more prominently than usual when placed twice in 2 days over C&D of late, probably doing a bit too much too soon when well backed most recently.

races.name: Happy 96th Birthday John Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: SPARTAN TIMES is still unexposed as a hurdler and looks well-in based on his recent Flat exploits, so he makes plenty of appeal. Jolie Coeur Allen wasn't beaten far over C&D on his most recent outing and should go well again with Charlie Maggs a positive jockey booking. Recent winner Cawthorne Cracker is also respected.

runners.note: Shrugged off any element of rustiness with a battling display when making a winning handicap hurdle debut at Uttoxeter in May. Run possibly came too soon at Aintree 13 days later and remains well treated on recent Flat e

Gained reward for her consistency when getting off the mark in a weakly-contested mares maiden at Fakenham (2m) in May. Probably needed the run (after 3 months off) when well held back on the level at Chester 18 days ago

Free-going front runner who got off the mark over C&D last October. Stepped up on her comeback run when second of 4 in handicap hurdle at Market Rasen (17f) in July and beaten less than a length over C&D since. Maggs a p
C&D winner who has been out of sorts on the Flat of late and fared little better back over hurdles at Stratford recently. Cheekpieces on for first time.

Caught the eye when third on handicap debut over hurdles at Market Rasen (16.6f) in May and again when filling the same spot back on the Flat at Catterick in July. Hasn't built on that promise since but possibly found th

Recorded a first success since landing this corresponding event in 2024 in 8-runner handicap hurdle at Kelso (2¼m, good) 13 days ago, edging ahead late on. Should remain competitive from a 4 lb higher mark.
Long-standing maiden who ran one of this season's better races when third in 10-runner handicap over C&D (good) 15 days ago. Not sure to be in the same form from 8 lb out of the weights, though.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
races.verdict: There is more to come from PINK VENOM after last week's Fairyhouse success and she can defy a 9 lb rise. Howlin Wolf continues to improve and looks the danger in new headgear.

runners.note: Beaten just 2¼ lengths in valuable 15-runner sales race at the Curragh earlier in the month but down the field in 7f Group 3 there on Sunday. Inflated mark to deal with now back in a nursery (held off 61 at Down Royal a
Well backed and much improved when second in maiden at Galway (7f, good) last month, but ran no sort of race at Down Royal next time. Drops to 6f with visor fitted for nursery debut.

Showed more dash than on his first 2 outings returning from a 9-week break (gelded) when third of 8 in 5f maiden at Navan at the start of the month. Not so good at Naas next time but could get back on track now handicapp
Boasts some good form and justified heavy support in making a successful nursery debut at Fairyhouse (6f) last week, suited by the strong pace. Another bold bid expected despite a 9 lb rise.
Improved when winning 5f Navan maiden 4 weeks ago, although possibly favoured by her position. 6f should suit but needs more again to defy her mark.

Improved with each run, getting off the mark switched to nurseries in 8-runner event at the Curragh in August and then twice second at Navan (6f), edged out in first-time cheekpieces last time. Stronger headgear on now a

Hasn't lived up to his pedigree/price tag but shaped better than the distance beaten suggests on second go in a nursery behind Pink Venom at Fairyhouse (6f) last week, showing plenty of speed in front and clear 2f out be

races.name: MJ Church Handicap
races.verdict: HEBRIDEAN NOMAD wasn't beaten far despite setting a strong pace at Lingfield last time so gets the vote in what looks a lesser race. Unexposed 3-y-os Zarco and Cosmo Brown are feared most.

runners.note: All 4 career victories at Wolverhampton, the latest over 1½m last summer. Largely creditable efforts in defeat this year, including when third here (1¾m, good to soft) 16 days ago. Likely to be on the premises again.
Had an excellent summer, completing a 4-timer last month. Probably wants the rain to stay away judged on her latest run here 16 days ago.

Finally opened his account in handicaps at Lingfield in January off a career-low mark. Not far off his very best when a close fourth there under this rider 17 days ago and can make presence felt again off the same mark i
Showed himself much happier back on the Flat when off the mark at Nottingham in July, pulling clear with the runner-up. Longer trip possibly stretched him at Newcastle (16.5f) next time.
Well backed and gained a first win for current yard here (11.6f) in July. However, well held next 2 starts (in refitted cheekpieces).
Has benefited from the switch to front running of late, making all in 4-runner event on the July Course. Similar form but only third of 5 back there since.
Best effort yet when second at Kempton on all-weather debut 5 weeks ago, shaping as if this step up in trip will suit. Player back in open company.
Went on a losing run for Alan King and is yet to fire for current yard.
Took advantage of career-low mark when opening account at Southwell a year ago. Returned with a decent third at Salisbury before winning a maiden over hurdles earlier this month.
All the better for return/handicap debut when close second at Lingfield 17 days ago, shaping as if this extra 1f will be within reach. Needs considering as an unexposed 3-y-o.

Scored twice on the level in 2024, including over 2m 1f here. Raced only once on the Flat thereafter but scored over hurdles at Fontwell in December. Arrives here after 2 respectable efforts in that sphere but that was i

Stepped forward from this season's return when scoring here (1¾m) in May and has gone close twice since, headed only in the dying strides at Epsom in July. Adopted different tactics to usual when down the field here next
Two wins at Ffos Las last summer. Best effort this year when close second of 4 at Nottingham in July but not in same form at Lingfield following month.
Standout effort when fourth on handicap debut at Salisbury in July. Down the field on both subsequent starts (in first-time headgear last time).

races.name: Weddings At Western House Hotel Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: The drop back in trip should suit LUNA LACY, who was too free when a promising fifth at Musselburgh earlier this month. She gets the nod. What A Girl Wants has proven expensive to follow but looks the obvious danger nonetheless.

runners.note: Well held in maiden (40/1) at Thirsk (6f, good) on debut 46 days ago. One for the longer term.
Foaled March 6. 27,000 gns yearling, £50,000 2-y-o, Naval Crown colt. Half-brother to 3 winners, including 2-y-o 5f-6f winner Kool Moe Dee and 1m winner Hatadora. Market check advised on debut.
Went with little immediate promise in maiden (50/1) at Musselburgh (7f, good to firm) on debut 17 days ago.
Failed to beat a rival home in maiden at Hamilton (5f, good to soft) on debut 27 days ago. Likely to need more time.
Twice-raced filly who shaped much better than bare result when fifth of 9 in maiden at Musselburgh (7f, good to firm, 33/1) 17 days ago, doing too much too soon. Should have more to offer.

Hasn't progressed/looked entirely straightforward since a promising start in Ireland in the spring but made the frame again, on second start for Nigel Tinkler, when second of 6 in novice at Pontefract (6f, good to soft,

races.name: Roxyfet Sports Lounge For Private Hire Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: STEEL RAVEN has been progressing well since upped to 1¼m+ on the Flat and appeals as the type to take well to hurdling. He's preferred to Jerseygeordie, who made much more impact tried over hurdles than in a handful of starts on all-weather for Jamie Osborne when third at Newton Abbot last month, form which has already been franked by the first 2. Watcha Snoop may prove best of the rest.

runners.note: Well held in 1m Kempton maiden on sole outing on the Flat for Andrew Balding in late 2025 but is a half-brother to 4 winners, including useful hurdler/chaser Plinth (2m-2¾m winner, by Montjeu), so it's reasonable to beli

Showed nothing in a handful of starts on all-weather for Jamie Osborne but made more impact tried over hurdles after 6 months off when third of 7 in a Newton Abbot juvenile (17f, good) 22 days ago. That form has since be
Son of Massaat who didn't go unsupported but ran out 2 from home (a length in front at time) on Newton Abbot hurdling debut in June. However, sent off 25/1 when well beaten at Uttoxeter since.
Fairly useful 1¼m winner on Flat (stays 11f) who ran really well when second in 11-runner handicap at Ayr (1¼m, soft) 12 days ago, finishing with running left. Likely type for juvenile hurdling.

Modest form in 1¼m handicaps on Flat. Given a considerate introduction to hurdling when fourth of 6 in same race contested by Watcha Snoop at Cartmel (17f) in August and likely to be brought along gradually.
Regressive sprinter on Flat and his second on hurdling debut at Cartmel (17f) last month probably says more about the worth of the race overall. Remains to be seen if he's able to build on that.
Poor maiden at up to 1m on the Flat who makes little appeal on this switch to hurdling.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap
races.verdict: BY THE LAKE is taken to build on her promising handicap/stable debut last month and strike under Colin Keane. Flash of Fire made a positive start for the Johnny Murtagh stable when fourth at Punchestown a fortnight ago and is taken to build on that and provide the chief threat ahead of Staysound Susie, who won this in 2024 and would be very much at home should the ground go soft/heavy.

runners.note: Won this in 2024 and scored at the Curragh (6f, heavy) in April. Probably needed a recent outing there after 4 months off and should be sharper now. Any further easing of the ground in her favour.
Dual winner for Ger Lyons as a juvenile. Made a positive reappearance for new yard when narrowly denied at Navan (6f, good) 33 days ago. Considered under Keane.
Won at Doncaster on debut. 11/1, first run since leaving James Ferguson when good fourth of 14 in handicap at Punchestown (1m, good) 14 days ago. Cheekpieces on first time. Respected.
Successful on second of 2 starts in maidens for Jarlath P. Fahey and even better form when third in handicaps over 7f/1m for new yard. Drops back 2f in trip now.
Sligo maiden winner on reappearance in May. Below-form fifth on 6f Fairyhouse handicap debut later that month. Given a break since. Retains potential for top stable.
Promise on first 2 starts before making it third time lucky in maiden at Down Royal (5f, good, evens) 25 days ago, always holding on. Makes handicap debut from a mark which demands improvement.
Mayson filly who was much improved from her debut when second of 11 in 6f maiden at Dundalk last year. Has a lengthy break to overcome on handicap debut.
Showed plenty of promise when runner-up on debut at the Curragh last summer but hasn't built on that in 4 subsequent runs.
Fourteen runs since last win in 2025. Reacted well to cheekpieces when second of 27 at the Curragh last month but the headgear hasn't worked as well since.

races.name: AEL Solutions Handicap
races.verdict: BUCKLAND BELLE can land the fourth win of a very productive season. Rating has a solid C&D record and heads the dangers along with Amarachi and Chilly Breeze.

runners.note: Capitalised on a falling mark under an enterprising ride at Salisbury (1m, good) last month but well held back there twice since.
C&D winner in May and added to tally at Chepstow (1m, good) in August. Creditable third of 10 over C&D (good to soft) 16 days ago. Likely to be in the mix again.
Runner-up twice over 1m on good to firm this summer and it may to overlook a lesser run on soft ground at Chester last time.
Three-time C&D winner, including back to back at the start of this summer. Well below par back here 16 days ago, though.
Dual winner who joined present yard for only 1,000 gns from Michael Dods last autumn and hasn't gone on from his reappearance fourth at Ffos Las.
More than hinted at ability in 3 outings over 1m last year but well beaten on 11f Kempton handicap debut/reappearance in June. Drops back in trip after a further 111 days off.
Produced a career best to get off the mark for this yard by a wide margin over C&D earlier this month. Backed it up with a creditable second of 12 at Wolverhampton (8.6f) 3 days later. Respected.
First run since leaving George Boughey when last of 9 in handicap (28/1) at Southwell (7f) 26 days ago. Can only watch after that.

Has won 3 times since switched to turf this year, pulling a little way clear with an in-form rival when landing the odds in 11-runner contest over C&D under Tom Marquand at the beginning of this month. Good second of 10
Has 11 course wins to name, including 2 more this summer. Narrowly denied by Buckland Belle over C&D at the beginning of this month but posted a rare below-par effort back here since.
Back from an absence to finish well held at Salisbury in August 2025 and off again since. First run for yard after leaving Mark Gillard. A watching brief is advised.

Resumed winning ways over C&D (firm) in July. Creditable third of 7 at Windsor next time but his run of good form came to a halt when well behind Buckland Belle and stablemate Blue Hero here 4 weeks ago.
Made all at Brighton in June but below par in her 3 outings since.
Maiden. 25/1, creditable third of 10 in handicap at Epsom (8.5f, good) 19 days ago. Less exposed than a lot of these.

races.name: Nairns's Oatcakes Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: Plenty to consider but KEEP AN EYE ON IT was unlucky not to beat his elders at Carlisle 6 weeks ago and can make amends with trip/ground unlikely to be an issue. Star Cast, Kokanee and Mehmas Champion all rate serious threats.

runners.note: Finally came good for this yard when causing a big surprise with a 80/1 win at Haydock 4 weeks ago, a strong gallop back on softer ground looking in his favour. Pulled clear with a subsequent winner that day and he remai
On the go since the turn of the year and gained a superb sixth win of 2026 over C&D (soft) in June. Has reached the frame from this career-high mark all 3 starts since and this looks slightly easier.

Maiden in Ireland for Johnny Murtagh but was placed on several occasions. Made a good start for new connections (sold 48,000 gns) when third over C&D last month, catching the eye with how he travelled. Reportedly sufferi
Right back to his best with testing ground proving ideal when winning at Lingfield off 1 lb lower in June. Not in the same form under quicker conditions since but going is now in his favour.

Forward-going type. Held on gamely to notch her fourth win of the season at Musselburgh in June and has mostly remained in good form, drop back to 1m probably against her at Hamilton 9 days ago. Headgear on.
Gained a first handicap success at Pontefract off this mark in April but has matched that form only once since, albeit when the ground was testing again. Goes beyond 1m for the first time.
Placed twice off similar marks last autumn and built on return 10 weeks later when fourth at Sandown. Ground in his favour and likely to go well.
Enhanced a fine Ripon record when doubling his tally for the year early this month. Hasn't been competitive away from that track this season, though, including last time.

Shown plenty of promise since switched to handicaps, winning here (1m) in August after a 4-month break. Unlucky not to follow up taking on his elders for the first time at Carlisle 6 weeks ago (conceding first run) and h

races.name: Paxtons No1 CaseIH Dealer Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: TANKING ALONG was let down by his jumping at Cartmel last time, but he'd been in notably in good form prior to that, so is well worth another chance for an in-form stable. Passengerontheship is narrowly preferred to Thank You Blue for forecast purposes.

runners.note: Brought up a quick-fire 5-timer in May/June (4 wins at Hexham). Got back on track after a couple of lesser efforts when second of 3 in 3m handicap at Warwick last week, though made quite hard work of things.

Enthusiastic front runner who opened his account over fences here in March and found only one too good on both starts in May, latterly in 6-runner handicap chase at Perth (2½m, soft), collared only on the run-in. Let dow

Completed a quick-fire hat-trick over hurdles at Ludlow in February. Not the most fluent jumper over fences but again ran well when beaten only a length in 8-runner handicap here in August. Seemed not to stay the much lo
Half-sister to a smart chaser but recent efforts uninspiring, including on debut over fences at Worcester (2m) last time. Step back up in trip needs to bring about improvement.

races.name: WTW Willis Handicap (0-60)
races.verdict: VERIFIED has gone close off higher marks, including at this track, and is chanced in the hope it can all come together back from a break in refitted headgear. El Fontenaro, Simmering Seas and last year's winner Ukiyo are all in the picture too.

runners.note: Had twice gone close before finally opening her account in C&D handicap 10 weeks ago. That form is solid for the grade and she can go well again after a 4 lb rise.
Doubled his tally in 5f handicap here in May and back from a break after lesser efforts the last twice. Unproven beyond the minimum trip.
Much improved in 2025, winning 3 times, but has underachieved this season. On a good mark if reviving.
Yet to win but shaping up nicely for new yard, in the frame again at Navan (5f) last time. Tongue tie back on and one to note.
Little form, well beaten again on handicap debut at Navan when last seen in June.
Losing run is mounting up but placed again with blinkers back on when third at Listowel (7f) last week.
Successful twice over 5f last year, but little encouragement since latest win. Has been given a big chance by the handicapper and has gone well here in the past.
Little impact in 3 races at Dundalk. Makes handicap/turf debut back from 8 months off.

Long-standing maiden handicapper who was a good second at Down Royal (5f) in June and can have his next run at Navan overlooked (short of room approaching final 1f and eased off). Placed on 3 of his 4 visits to Cork and
Maiden who left E. J. O'Neill cheaply and shaped as if better for the run back from 11 months off at Naas. Could build on that and not had much racing in handicaps.
Third in a strong Navan maiden on sole start at 2 yrs, but having missed all of her 3-y-o season she hasn't progressed. Down in class back from 5 months off.

Never looked like justifying support on rare start over the minimum trip at Hamilton 7 weeks ago but had previously reached the frame 4 times this season and returns from a break bidding to win this race for the second y
Yet to win but ran well on her first start in a sprint handicap when third at Laytown (6f) earlier this month. Not out of it if building on that.
C&D winner in 2023 but lightly raced this year and ran poorly back from 3 months off here recently. Drops back to a sprint trip now.

Ran well in first-time cheekpieces when fifth of 16 in 1m handicap here last month, albeit not fully convincing with his stamina for the longer trip. Didn't look the easiest of rides at Listowel (7f) since, however. Stro
Lightly-raced maiden who hasn't improved in handicaps this year, including tried in blinkers. Cheekpieces go on now.
Remains a maiden and failed to build on a couple of better efforts when down the field at Limerick (1m) when last seen 3 months ago, a gamble on him going west.

Won C&D handicap last season and having been in a slump since, offered a bit more back here in July in refitted headgear. Best not judged on subsequent Clonmel run over much further (headway when badly hampered entering
Won this in 2023 and 2024 for different trainers but looks to have lost his way.

Blinkered for the first time when getting off the mark in 6f handicap at Sligo in August. That form was franked but he wasn't in the same mood in cheekpieces at Listowel last week. No headgear on this time.

races.name: British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: DIVIDE AND CONQUER went close to landing a gamble at Ascot on debut so is preferred to Al Qayed, who looks more of a 3-y-o prospect.

runners.note: Stepped up on debut when third in heavy-ground maiden at Goodwood 3 weeks ago, not knocked about (form is working out well). A raw, rather backward type, he should have more to offer.

3,000 gns yearling, Cracksman colt. Dam unraced half-sister to very smart 6f winner Shalaa out of 2-y-o 6f winner (stayed 9.7f) Ghurra. Could hardly have shown any less in Lingfield maiden last month and headgear now app

Tasleet colt. Half-brother to Australian 1m winner General Bordeaux and winner up to 1¾m Dance Havana (a 2-y-o 9f winner). Dam, 11.6f winner, half-sister to smart 1m winner Trade Commissioner. Very green when well held i

Foaled March 30. New Bay colt. Half-brother to 1¾m-2m winner Tactician and 1½m winner Desert Spring, both useful. Dam, 13.3f winner, closely related to winner up to 1¼m Midas Touch and dual Group 1 winner Coronet (both v

320,000 gns Camelot half-sister to 1¼m winner Time Thief. Dam smart 1m winner. Well backed when neck second in Ascot maiden early this month, just edged out by one with experience. Strongly fancied to go one better.

Foaled February 7. New Bay filly. Closely related to smart French 1¼m-1½m winner Ambition and 1¼m winner Pretty Fair. Dam, winner up to 1½m (including Oaks, also 2-y-o 7f winner) who stayed 14.5f, half-sister to very sma

races.name: Autumn Breaks At Western House Hotel Handicap
races.verdict: The in-form HOMESTRAIT ran a cracker in a stronger contest at Chester last time and can race off the same mark here. She makes fair appeal. Misunderstood and One NIght Thunder rate the principal dangers.

runners.note: His smart 2-y-o form seems a thing of the past but he figures off a handy mark and has been performing with credit of late, a bit too keen when fifth at Beverley over this trip last week. Shortlisted.
Produced a career best when scoring at Carlisle (7f, good to soft) last month but not been in quite same form since. Others preferred.
Well over a year since his last win but he ran another fine race when second of 15 in handicap at York (7f) earlier this month and had excuses over C&D since (not clear run). Respected.
Dual 7f winner this year who has found a little more improvement in recent starts, latest when good third of 8 in handicap at Chester (7f, heavy) 10 days ago. Merits consideration.

Dual winner at 7f this season, most recently at Musselburgh in April. Largely run well since, making the frame once more when third of 8 in handicap at Hamilton (6f, soft, 10/1) 8 days ago. Likely to be in the mix again.
Built on debut promise to gamely land 10-runner maiden at Thirsk (7f) in June. Disappointed in testing conditions on handicap debut at Haydock since but remains low mileage.
Won at Doncaster on 2025 reappearance but has rarely threatened since, well held at same course when last seen in July. Work to do.
Not successful since 2024 and has largely struggled for form this season. Visor reapplied now but he is hard to recommend with confidence despite a tumbling mark.
Dual Carlisle winner last season who stepped up on recent efforts when creditable third of 10 in handicap at same course (7f, good to soft, 7/2) 20 days ago. 1 lb lower now and is not taken lightly.
Gained a breakthrough victory over C&D in June but only tenth of 12 in handicap in follow-up attempt here since. Bounce back is required.

races.name: Sedgefield Racecourse For Outdoor Events Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: HIJO DE LA LUNA's recent form looks sound and he's taken to notch a breakthrough win over hurdles. Whitewinewednesday had excuses on her first start for her all-conquering yard at Limerick in May and remains one to keep an eye on given her previous promise, while Vanilla Dancer is the type to bounce back quickly from a below-par display when last seen.

runners.note: Veteran who resumed winning ways at Cartmel (17.2f) in July and has confirmed himself still in top form on both subsequent outings, finishing third to a couple of stablemates at Bangor (2½m) latest. 10-lb claimer back in

A fair and lightly-raced maiden on Flat in first half of 2024. Returned from 17 months off and displayed aptitude for hurdling when third of 9 here (16.8f) here last December but well held at Wetherby 3 weeks later and a

Broke duck over hurdles when winning at Catterick (2m) in February and performed well in defeat next 3 outings. Produced a rare below-par effort at Kelso when last seen in May and very much the type to bounce back quickl

Hasn't kicked on after a promising start in handicaps but can have her first run for Willie Mullins at Limerick in May overlooked having raced on unfavoured inside and later said to be showing signs of being in season. T

Regressive maiden on the Flat who made more impact than previously over hurdles when ¾-length second in a C&D novice in August. However, struggled in his first handicap in this sphere back over C&D since, an SP of 28/1 a
Confirmed he still has something to offer when third of 8 in handicap hurdle at Kelso (2¼m, good) 13 days ago. Recent form sound and must enter the reckoning.

Not seen to best effect on most recent Flat outing and was again caught further back than ideal when third of 9 in handicap hurdle over C&D (firm, 4/1) 32 days ago. Merits consideration from 1 lb lower mark.
Maiden who was possibly unsuited by the drop back in trip when fifth of 10 in handicap hurdle at this course (17f, firm, 20/1) last month, though still has little in the way of form.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Navigation Stakes (Listed)
races.verdict: SUMMER IS TOMORROW has improved since a visor went on and looks well worth another shot at this level. Shaihaan is feared most back down in class, while Latin America is the potential improver in the field.

runners.note: Smart effort when second in the Dante at York in May but mainly used as a pacemaker since, often having hard races. Difficult to know how much ability/enthusiasm he retains.
Showed plenty in Punchestown maidens a year apart, landing the odds in a tongue strap 2 weeks ago. This much harder but he remains with potential.
Seemingly much improved when thrashing his 4 rivals off a mark of 72 at Gowran in June. Off since and will find this much more demanding.

Gleneagles colt who confirmed debut promise (second to Shaihaan) when landing the odds in 18-runner maiden at Navan in April. Shaped well considering the drop in trip seemed to be against him in a useful event at Naas th
Sea The Stars colt who hails from a fine staying family and confirmed debut promise when winning Roscommon maiden 6 weeks ago. Looks useful but drop in trip is likely to find him out at this level.

Remains steadily progressive and got off the mark for the year at Killarney last month. Beaten only by a smart prospect in the Irish Cambridgeshire the following week and produced another solid effort off 10 lb higher at
Heavy-ground maiden winner at Gowran last autumn. Better form in defeat this season but this looks another stiffish task. Has since been gelded.
Convincing winner of Curragh maiden on reappearance but highly tried after. This looks more his level and easier going could also be a plus. Has been gelded.

Dual winner at 2 yrs who has improved since fitted with a visor, landing the odds by a wide margin at Gowran before an excellent fourth of 22 off a mark of 102 at the Curragh 16 days ago. Looks more than ready for this l
Found improvement when winning listed race at Naas in May and better form when making the frame in Group 2 and Group 3s since. Respected back down in class despite her penalty.

Ended last season with back-to-back wins in a Killarney maiden and valuable sales race at Naas. Struggled on handicap debut/Group 3 races in the spring but yard is going much better now and she resumed progress back from
Runner-up to stablemates both starts last year and went one better in a maiden at Cork on return. However, limitations seemingly exposed in Group 3 at the Curragh last month.

races.name: SW Hire Handicap
races.verdict: SOUTH SHORE continues to thrive for his current yard and his latest win at Sandown looks rock solid given what the re-opposing Maharajas Express has since achieved. Brave Nation completes the shortlist having made a bright start for Michael Attwater.

runners.note: Resumed winning ways in good style here (5.7f) in May, a first success on turf. Not in the same form off revised mark next 2 starts but she looked back to her best after a short break when runner-up at Lingfield, likely

Has thrived this summer, winning over C&D and Newbury before making it 3 wins from 4 starts at Chester, defying a double-figure draw. Always behind back there since but that was on much softer ground.
C&D winner last autumn and back to winning ways here (5.7f) in June. Not so good over 6f on next 2 starts but returned to form back at 5f when placed at Nottingham and Goodwood.
Progressive last season, winning 3 times. Has struggled in a light campaign this time around, though latest effort at Lingfield was a bit more encouraging.
Returned to her best to deny a well-treated rival for a first success on turf at Doncaster 3 months ago. Off since but she has won off a break before.

Without a win for Michael Bell in 2025, but after an encouraging first run for this yard he got his head back in front at Newmarket early last month. Easy to forgive latest run at Goodwood and he remains well treated on

Revitalised for new yard, winning on stable debut at Windsor and following up at Wolverhampton 7 days later. Runner-up next 3 starts before resuming winning ways at Sandown by ¾ length from Maharajas Express. Back up in
C&D winner who has looked better than ever of late, close second of 21 at York before going one better at Doncaster last time. Must be respected in current mood.

Off the mark at Windsor in May and doubled his tally in 4-runner contest at Nottingham in July. Found Glorious Goodwood too much to handle next time and was stretched back over 6f since, so no surprise if he fared better
Fitted with cheekpieces, was making only his second start over 5f when getting off the mark at Windsor in May. Backed that up when second over C&D but has plenty to prove now after 2 poor efforts.
Sole success came in a C&D nursery off this mark this time last year under this rider. Good efforts when runner-up twice in a week at Goodwood this summer but not at that level in 3 starts since.

Bred to be speedy and didn't need to improve to get off the mark in 4-runner maiden at Chepstow (6f, soft) last month. Disappointed on handicap/all-weather debut at Kempton since and this is a much better race.

races.name: Book Your Event At Ayr Racecourse Handicap
races.verdict: HIGHFIELD VIKING bounced back to form when third over C&D 12 days ago and he's well treated if building on that with conditions in his favour once again. Showtown is another who revived last time and is next best ahead of fellow 3-y-o Lope Y Linda.

runners.note: Capitalised on a much-reduced mark to snap a long losing run on turf at Musselburgh. Unable to open up fully at Thirsk since but he has been kept away from testing ground for most of his career.

Back-to-back winner last summer (including over C&D). Struggled after an encouraging reappearance but took a big step back in the right direction off reduced mark when third over C&D (soft) 12 days ago and well treated i
Maiden who was runner-up 3 times in a row earlier in the season, but not quite at those levels since. Blinkers now go on.
Maiden who bounced back to form from his slipping mark when beaten only by a gambled-on winner at Thirsk 2 weeks ago, clear of the rest and seeing out this longer trip well. Not taken lightly.

Perked up with the application of headgear when off the mark at Catterick before backing that up when fourth here (1m). Ran well without the headgear at Yarmouth 12 days ago but not an obvious type to handle bad ground.
Maiden but often gives his running and looked rusty after 5 months off at Redcar 3 weeks ago.

Free-going type who looked better than ever when making all at Catterick 3 weeks ago, her rider doing well to get across from the widest stall. 5 lb rise seems a little excessive but she has a good record here.
Not the force of old and further decline this year, though at least fared better for a while when third here (1m) 22 days ago, albeit beaten almost 5 lengths.
Ex-Irish 4-y-o who has yet to win a handicap and hasn't cut much ice for current yard.

Sole success came in Bath novice (heavy) for Marcus Tregoning in autumn 2024. Hasn't threatened to capitalise on slipping mark since joining this yard, her latest run here particularly poor. Cheekpieces back on.
Poor maiden who is easy to oppose.

races.name: Premier Road Markings Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: JET OF DREAMS quite possibly needed the run after a 4-month break at Uttoxeter recently and having been given a chance by the handicapper, is a tentative selection to repeat his win in this race last year. Mary gives the impression she'll benefit from this return to shorter and is feared most.

runners.note: Impressive all-the-way winner of a Worcester novice hurdle on stable debut last summer and back in similar heart when making the frame in handicaps this season. Failed to meet expectations sent chasing after an unconvinc

Registered a fifth career victory over fences in this corresponding event last year. Patchy form since, though possibly needed run after 4 months off at Uttoxeter last time and back down to a good mark.

Thriving over hurdles and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat when completing a hat-trick at Newton Abbot in June. Ran her best race over fences when fourth of 8 at Uttoxeter a fortnight ago but lacks size and remai

Looked set to go close again when taking another late fall in a novice handicap chase at Bangor in May. Has shaped as if still in good form on both subsequent outings and is likely to benefit from this drop back in trip.
Has shown little sign of a return to form following a breathing operation, including back over hurdles last time. Others preferred.

races.name: Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (Smullen Series)
races.verdict: This has the makings of a really interesting maiden with GOLDEN RING taken to make her experience count and get off the mark, this step up to 1m promising to unlock further improvement. Gods Love, Duchessofaquitaine and Somebody Loves Me, a stablemate of the selection, head up a host of appealing newcomers.

runners.note: Foaled April 13. New Bay filly. Half-sister to useful 1¼m winner Alazenya. Dam, 1½m winner, half-sister to very smart 1½m-2½m winner Alandi.
Foaled March 2. Invincible Army filly. Dam unraced. Starts out in a tough maiden.

Foaled March 2. Wootton Bassett filly. Sister to very smart winner up to 10.2f Whirl. Dam, 1m winner, sister to winner up to 12.4f The United States and winner up to 1½m Hydrangea (both very smart) out of smart winner up

Foaled May 9. Dubawi filly. Half-sister to winner up to 11f New World Tapestry and 2-y-o 7f/1m winner Dreamy, both useful. Dam winner up to 1½m (Yorkshire Oaks, also won at 6f/7f at 2 yrs) out of smart 2-y-o winner up to

220,000 gns yearling, Baaeed filly. Half-sister to several winners, including useful winner up to 2m Kirchner and 6f winner Angel Girl. Promising first effort when sixth of 14 in 1m Punchestown maiden (28/1) a fortnight
Foaled March 8. Awtaad filly. Half-sister to several winners, including useful 2-y-o 7f/1m winner Washaar and 11.6f-1¾m winner Celtic Classic. Dam placed sole start.

Foaled April 11. 425,000 gns yearling, Sea The Stars filly. Sister to smart winner up to 1m The Lion In Winter. Dam, 1½m/12.3f winner, half-sister to smart 1¼m-1½m winner Venus de Milo. Appealing newcomer on paper and pl

Foaled January 27. 525,000 gns yearling, Dubawi filly. Sister to 1½m winner King's Reign and half-sister to smart winner up to 1½m Silver Knott. Dam, 1¼m-1¾m winner (won Park Hill Stakes and Premio Lydia Tesio), half-sis

Wootton Bassett filly is a half-sister to several winners, including very smart Armory (2-y-o 7f winner). Proved well suited by step up to 7f and much improved when 4 lengths third of 17 in maiden here 3 weeks ago. 1m wi

Foaled January 29. 250,000 gns yearling, Lope De Vega filly. Half-sister to 1m-10.4f winner Highland Spring and 11f-1½m winner in Germany Dawn Sky. Dam winner up to 10.5f (2-y-o 1m/9f winner). Sixth of 8 in barrier trial

€75,000 foal, €78,000 yearling, Camelot filly. Dam 2-y-o 7f winner. 150/1, mid-field in 7f Gowran maiden on debut 4 weeks ago. Should know more this time but will probably make little appeal this side of handicaps.
Not unbacked but shaped as if in need of the experience when eighth in 21-runner 6f Naas maiden 12 days ago. Longer trip here should suit. Engaged 2.34 Down Royal Monday.

Foaled February 21. 800,000 gns foal, Frankel filly. Closely related to 12.5f winner Dusk Falls and half-sister to several winners, including winner up to 1m Cloudy Dawn. Dam 1m/9f winner. 1 of 4 runners for Aidan O'Brie

Foaled March 25. €115,000 yearling, State of Rest filly. Half-sister to 2-y-o 7f winner Orne and 1¼m winner Alcarath, both useful. Dam, winner up to 6.5f, half-sister to smart winner up to 1m Space Traveller.
Foaled April 10. Ardad filly. Half-sister to 1m winner Lightning Glory. Dam, ran twice at 2 yrs, half-sister to useful US 1m/9f winner K P All Systems Go.
Well drawn and showed more than first time up when fifth in 17-runner 7f maiden here 3 weeks ago. 1m will suit but might be more one for handicaps over even further next year.

races.name: Hotel & Conferencing At Wolverhampton Handicap
races.verdict: The draw could have been kinder to HENFIELD but she caught the eye with her strong finish at Lingfield last time and gets the nod ahead of Manton Road, another who shaped well from too far back on his latest start.  It's A Love Thing can also play a part if able to back up his latest Newcastle third.

runners.note: Course winner in spring 2025. On a long losing run but much better signs after 4 months off with third of 7 in handicap at Newcastle (1¼m) 27 days ago. Claims if he can back that up.
Ended a losing run here (7f) in July and remained in form since, including third of 12 over 8.6f here 14 days ago, shaping quite well having been poorly placed. Considered.
Successful 4 times on all-weather this year, latest over C&D on April. Not at the top of her game when last seen at the start of the summer, though.

Tends to start slowly but did get off the mark in 1m classified event at Lingfield under Billy Loughnane in July. Hasn't reproduced that level in 2 handicaps but the return of Loughnane to the saddle is a plus.
Winless in 12 starts, beating just one home again in handicap at Southwell (1m) 44 days ago. Wears first-time cheekpieces.
Successful twice over C&D last winter but has gone off the boil since.
Second at Chepstow (1m) in July but not at that level in 3 outings since.
Showed promise when third over C&D in February. Well held on next 2 outings but took a step back in the right direction for new yard when third of 6 at Leicester (1¼m, good to firm) last month.

Won 1m classified race at Lingfield in July. Even better form when second of 9 in handicap there 17 days ago, staying on strongly from too far back. The outside stall isn't ideal but she's still the one to beat.
Long-standing maiden. Back to form in refitted cheekpieces for new yard when fourth of 9 in handicap at Newcastle (1m) 27 days ago. Needs to back it up with headgear retained.
No impact in his 4 handicap starts and needs to find improvement from somewhere.
Modest form in 6 outings for Ollie Sangster and only seventh of 12 over 8.6f here on stable debut 3 weeks ago.
Lightly-raced maiden who's yet to show a great deal from 5 starts.

races.name: Power Logistics Nursery
races.verdict: HEMUSTBEANANGEL shaped quite well on his 7f nursery debut and can come good back over shorter for in-form Roger Teal. Devon Angel has been runner-up on her last 2 starts and rates an obvious danger. Snow On The Beach is with an excellent stable and rates a potential improver in her first handicap.

runners.note: Proving a consistent sort and ran with credit again when third of 14 in nursery (5/1) at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 22 days ago. Likely to give her running again.

Promising type. 3/1, shaped better than result when sixth of 10 on nursery debut at Leicester (7f, good) 21 days ago, threatening out wide before his effort flattened out. Open to further progress back sprinting for in-f
Best effort (modest form) when second of 6 in a C&D maiden at Bath at the beginning of this month. Not in the same form in a nursery at Southwell since. Cheekpieces are added on the back of that.
Has shown a tendency to pull hard but in very good hands and likely improver in nurseries if learning to settle better.
Modest form in novices but last in both nurseries. A first-time tongue tie needs to spark an upturn in his fortunes.
Thrice-raced maiden. Sixth of 10 in novice at Wolverhampton (6f, 66/1) 14 days ago. Makes nursery debut.
This is her first nursery but she's seemingly exposed as modest after 9 starts.
Thrice-raced maiden. Last of 5 in maiden (150/1) at Chepstow (7f, good) 42 days ago. Has been gelded and makes handicap debut from a mark which demands improvement.
17/2 and visored first time, bit below form when eighth of 14 in nursery at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 22 days ago. Has a first-time tongue tie added to the visor now.
Creditable second of 14 in nursery at Windsor (6f, good to firm, 9/2) 22 days ago. Blinkers on first time. Likely to give another good account.
Hinted at ability in a Windsor novice (5f) on debut but hasn't kicked on in 4 outings since, including 2 nurseries.
Well held in novice/maidens at up to 7f in recent months. More chance now handicapping from a basement mark but still hard to be positive.

races.name: Book Racing On Saturday 31 October Handicap
races.verdict: Course winner ASHEN was clear of the rest when a good second at Hamilton last week and should appreciate the return to this longer trip. He gets the nod. Recent Hamilton scorer Belsito is feared most, whilst market strength behind the lightly-raced Big Harry again could prove significant.

runners.note: Posted career best when resuming winning ways in 8-runner handicap at Hamilton (6f, soft, 7/1) 8 days ago, driven out. Carries 5-lb penalty for that success but must enter calculations.
Scored here this time last year but been rather inconsistent this season, below form ninth of 24 in the Ayr Bronze Cup (soft) 11 days ago, merely closing up late. Others more persuasive.

Got better with each run at 2 yrs and ran out an easy winner of a heavy-ground 6f Doncaster novice on final start from Thunder Call (now rated 109). Disappointed on sole start in Kempton handicap this season (well backed
Posted best effort for a while when seventh at Ripon last month but failed to build on that behind Belsito at Hamilton since. Others more convincing.

Has his own way of doing things but suited by testing conditions and returned to form when creditable second of 14 in handicap at Haydock (6f, heavy, 5/1) 25 days ago. Claims if in the same mood and was runner-up in this
Resumed with success at Hamilton (5f) in June and back to form when a close third there on Monday, sticking to his task.
Took advantage of a drop back in grade when winning apprentice handicap at Carlisle in June. Below that level since, however, and has something to prove at present. Blinkers back on.

Not long with present stable when opening account at this course (7f) in May and largely held his form well since, producing another creditable effort when second of 6 in handicap at Hamilton (5f, soft) 8 days ago. Short

races.name: Fairlight Studios Cafe At Sedgefield Racecourse Open NH Flat Race (GBB Race)
races.verdict: CLOSE HOUSE showed plenty in what is usually a warm race at Ayr back in the spring and is a straightforward choice to get off the mark at the second time of asking. Red Shea was no match for a useful prospect at Cork last month but kept on to pull clear of the remainder and should at least give the selection something to think about if coping with the sharper test. Lower De Couely, an easy winner

runners.note: €11,500 3-y-o, Wings of Eagles gelding who made an encouraging start to his career when third of 9 in heavy-ground bumper at Ayr (2m) on sole outing for A. Slattery in April. That is a traditionally a strong race and he

Crystal Ocean gelding. Half-brother to 4 winners, including useful chaser Annie Angel. Produced a promising first effort when second of 17 at Cork (2¼m, good to soft) in August, albeit no match for the winner. Faces a sh
Postponed gelding. Dam (b79), ran once in bumper, half-sister to useful hurdler (stayed 2¾m) Babbling Stream.

No Risk At All mare. Sister to a winner on Flat and half-sister to 3 winners, including French chaser Kuflower de Couely. Easy winner of sole start in Irish points (May 2026) and one to note in the betting now switching

races.name: Follow Us On X Handicap
races.verdict: PLAYIN COOL has contested some warm handicaps this year and shaped encouragingly in the Irish Cambridgeshire last month. With his sights lowered after a 3 lb drop in the weights he could be set to play a prominent role. Karrygrant and Daler are big dangers.

runners.note: Lightly raced but useful at best for Charlie Appleby. Picked up for £64,000 by this yard but hasn't shown much in 2 runs for them.

Successful debut at the Curragh in March. Thrown in at the deep end for handicap debut in the Britannia at Royal Ascot latest start and found little off the bridle. Not seen since but remains unexposed.

Progressive form in maidens for Gavin Cromwell last season, getting off the mark in C&D contest in September. Successful return for new stable at Limerick in April and this is easier than the Irish Cambridgeshire he cont

Fairly useful filly who shaped as if back in form when third of 9 in handicap at Down Royal in June, seeming stretched by the 10.4f trip. Stiff task in first-time blinkers at Galway since and this is more her level.
Doubled his tally in 15-runner handicap at Leopardstown (9f) in June in first-time cheekpieces and has held his form well since. Can give another good account.
Low mileage 4-y-o shaped well again when fifth in the Irish Cambridgeshire last month, probably not ideally placed having sat off what was just an ordinary gallop. Interesting after a 3 lb drop.

Won 7f Fairyhouse maiden and 6f Naas novice (match) in June. Failed to justify strong market confidence but posted another creditable effort when third at the Curragh on Saturday, albeit once more looking less than strai
Winner of 1m maiden at Dundalk in March and had been running well in handicaps until a poor effort when sent off favourite at Gowran (9.5f) in June. Not ruled out after a break.

Odds on and placed once again when beaten just a nose in 1m Bellewstown maiden 5 weeks ago, a bit disappointing he couldn't get the job done having got to the front. Tongue tie goes on for handicap debut and probably set

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap
races.verdict: SEVENKINGSMUSTDIE is taken to build on his promising C&D handicap debut third and prove too strong for last week's Kempton scorer Arundel.

runners.note: Returned from a near year-long absence with an encouraging third at Yarmouth (1¼m, good) last month and  built on that with an 11f Kempton success under Billy Loughnane last Wednesday. Respected under a 5 lb-penalty.
Flat/hurdles winner who steadily eased in the weights following a low-key start to the season and back on form when runner-up over 1m at Newmarket and 1¾m at Southwell on his last 2 outings.
Snapped a losing run over 11f at Southwell 12 days ago. Only nudged up 2 lb so likely to be competitive again.
Dropped to a career-low mark but ran moderately when fifth of 8 at Redcar (1¼m, good) 38 days ago. Up in trip. One who needs things to drop right.

Showed fair form at start of his career but well held in 3 all-weather handicaps for Ben Brookhouse in winter 2024/25 and has a 20-month absence to overcome on first outing for Ian Williams. Could only consider if backed
Attracted support and shaped with promise when third of 6 on C&D handicap debut 4 weeks ago. There should be more to come from this lightly-raced sort.

races.name: Clyde And Co Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: DISTANT RUMBLE had plenty to spare at Windsor and is selected to make light of a 7 lb rise, perhaps at the expense of the thriving Legendsoftheland. Rumble Ruby and Control Room are others capable of having a say.

runners.note: Career best when winning 13-runner handicap at Windsor (6f, good, 5/1) 15 days ago, readily. Even a 7 lb rise may not stop him with Roger Teal continuing in excellent form.
Kickstarted 2026 with a C&D win off 2 lb higher in April. Respectable fourth of 9 in handicap at Goodwood (5f, good) 32 days ago. Enters calculations back here.
Scored at Beverley and close third at Yarmouth (both 5f) in quick succession in August. Not in the same form on Kempton's all-weather since but her turf record is solid.
Gained breakthrough on turf at Goodwood (5f) in May. Runner-up twice since and rather out of his pay grade in a Newbury Class 3 last time. This is more his level.
Won a Chepstow maiden last summer but she hasn't kicked on in handicaps this year, not convincing with her attitude in this headgear latest.
Ended long losing run when making most in 6-runner handicap at Goodwood (5f) this month but below-form sixth of 13 to Distant Rumble at Windsor since.
Confirmed debut promise at second time of asking when winning a 7f Chepstow maiden but no show in handicaps since. First-time cheekpieces and a return to sprinting need to spark a revival.

Consistent, front-running filly. Won a soft-ground Catterick maiden for Robert Cowell on final 2-y-o start. Has been running well in defeat for this yard, notably second of 10 at Sandown (5f, good to soft) last time.

Looked unlucky not to win when second of 4 at Chepstow last month, keeping on again after rider lost iron briefly last ½f. Stumbled leaving stalls when respectable fourth at Ffos Las next time and may have simply failed
Thriving sort who has won 3 times this year, including C&D. Another excellent effort when second of 17 over C&D (good to soft) 16 days ago. Should go well again.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap
races.verdict: Last year's winner AIGHEAR tends to save her best for this time of year and signalled a return to form at Hamilton earlier this month. She is fancied to land the finale. Time Turner and Furhaan should also go well.

runners.note: Ran right up to best, in first-time blinkers, when creditable second of 7 in handicap at Beverley (2m, heavy, 4/1) 30 days ago, keeping on gamely. Just 1 lb higher now and is one for the shortlist.

Drawn a blank since handicap debut success for Ed Walker last autumn but made the frame on several occasions this season, latest when creditable third of 10 in handicap over shorter trip at this course 11 days ago. Likel
Fair form when in the frame on her first 2 runs but disappointed since, including on Kempton handicap debut last month.
Four-time course winner, latest over shorter trip in July. Made the frame on next 2 starts but needs to bounce back from a poor run here 11 days ago.

Won this contest (off 6 lb lower) last year and followed up in convincing fashion here 10 days later. Yet to score this season but arrives on back of creditable fourth of 12 in handicap over shorter trip at Hamilton earl
Looked green but showed ability when third at Leicester on debut last October but still to better that form in 4 attempts since. Tries longer trip now but is hard to fancy.
Remains a maiden after 16 Flat runs and recent efforts haven't offered much encouragement. Visor back on.

races.name: Fitzgerald's Woodlands House Hotel Handicap (0-60)
races.verdict: CAUSE I LIKE YOU has run well over this trip since scoring at Killarney in July and gets the nod in an open-looking finale. Medieval Night and Monocle Rocket head the list of dangers.

runners.note: Still a maiden but he arrives in good form, making the frame again when creditable third of 14 in handicap at Clonmel (1¼m, good) 13 days ago. Likely to give another good account.
Comfortably scored at Roscommon in May. Largely in good form since until poor run at Listowel latest. Needs to bounce back.
Lightly-raced maiden who has cut little ice in 1m handicaps so far this season.
Lightly-raced maiden. 33/1, last of 16 in handicap at Navan (1m, good) 27 days ago, slowly away. Tongue strap on first time. Hard to fancy.
Consistent sort who posted another solid effort when fifth of 14 in handicap at Clonmel (1¼m, good) 13 days ago, running on. Ought to go well again.
Seventeen runs since last win in 2023 and ran poorly, back from 12 weeks off, in handicap at Galway (7f, soft) 21 days ago. Work to do.
Yet to trouble the judge in 6 attempts, including tried in blinkers over longer trip at Sligo latest. Tongue strap on first time. Makes limited appeal.

Well held in 3 turf maidens for Henry de Bromhead last summer but more promising signs for new yard when second in Gowran handicap (7f) on return in April. Below that level at same course later that month but warrants re
Lightly-raced maiden who shaped better than distance beaten when respectable twelfth of 21 in handicap (20/1) at Navan (1¼m, good) 24 days ago. This shorter trip may suit.

Winner at Bellewstown (1m) in July. In and out since but shaped better than distance beaten when tenth of 22 in handicap at this course (7f, soft) 20 days ago, finishing with running left. Not discounted.
Off the mark at Killarney (1m) in July and back to that sort of form when good second of 16 in handicap (8/1) at Gowran (1m, soft) 10 days ago. Shortlist material.
Back from break when scoring at Dundalk in July. Seems to save her best for that course, though, well held at Laytown (7f, 7/2) 19 days ago. Others preferred.
Still looking for first success but posted another respectable effort when sixth of 10 in handicap at Laytown (7f) 19 days ago. Each-way claims.
Has yet to progress from his debut including on switch to handicaps at the Curragh latest.
Well held in maidens in 2024/25. Not seen for 10 months and likely best watched on handicap debut for new yard here. Tongue strap on first time.
Late headway when respectable sixth of 14 in handicap (9/2) at Punchestown (9f, good) 14 days ago but losing run continues to grow.
Well supported but finished well held in handicap at Clonmel (1¼m, good) 13 days ago. Fairly treated on best form, though.
Promise in Dundalk handicaps earlier this year but gone backwards since.
Didn't show much in 3 starts for Richard Hannon (sold for 11,000gns) and similar story on debut for new yard at Gowran 10 days ago. RESERVE.
Back-to-back handicap winner on the Flat last autumn but more miss than hit since although had little chance in listed company latest. Claims on best form. RESERVE.
Losing run stretches back to 2023 and was well beaten at Down Royal on Monday. RESERVE.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: ARABIAN SUMMER made her debut in quite a useful contest at Kempton a couple of years ago. It's taken a long time to get her back but plenty from this stable have overcome long absences down the years and she gets the vote with confidence in her chance increased should the betting vibes be strong. Battlefield Boy shaped with encouragement on his recent debut and is feared most ahead of Gold Star Ga

runners.note: Showed some ability in bumpers but more one for handicaps in this sphere based on his 2 Kempton outings in recent weeks.
Promising individual. 7/1, third of 8 in maiden at Lingfield (1m, all-weather) on debut 19 days ago, clear of rest. Likely to improve and considered under Loughnane.

2/1, green when fifth of 10 in novice at Southwell (1m) on debut last November. The fact he was prominent in the betting suggests better was anticipated. It'll be interesting to see whether he attracts support again on r
Fair maiden. Visored first time (retained), creditable 2 lengths second of 4 in 6f Lingfield novice 4 weeks ago. Likely to be on the premises again.
150/1, twelfth of 13 in maiden at Southwell (7f) on debut 68 days ago.
Comfortably held in a pair of 7f outings at Kempton last month.
4/1, showed a fair level of ability when sixth of 10 in novice at Kempton (6f) on debut in October 2024. Not seen since but a long absence is often no barrier to success with horses from this yard.

Sergei Prokofiev half-sister to 1½m-16.6f winner Glorious Dane. Dam, 2-y-o 1m winner, half-sister to useful 2-y-o 7.5f winner (stayed 9.5f) On Verra. The betting is the best guide to expectations on this belated debut.
It took a while to get her to the track but she showed some promise when third of 8 in 6f Kempton novice 15 days ago. Likely to progress.
Well held on C&D debut for Jack Morland in July. Offered a bit more for new yard at Kempton 45 days later but not enough to suggest she can make an impact here.
Too Darn Hot half-sister to winner up to 6f Nezeeh. Dam 5f winner who stayed 7f. It'll be interesting to see how she compares in the betting to stablemate Arabian Summer.

races.name: Clyde And Co Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: Three-time C&D winner MOE'S LEGACY could be ready to strike off a winning mark, especially if the rain stays away. Charlie Boyo is well worth another chance so is second choice ahead of fellow 3-y-o Guilty Verdict, whose Salisbury form has worked out very well.

runners.note: Showed improved form to get off the mark up against older rivals for the first time at Nottingham in July, overcoming a slow start. Too free in a small field the following week so he's well worth another chance.

Narrow winner of a 2-y-o maiden at Leicester and proved all the better for his return when runner-up in this headgear at Ffos Las last month. However, that form hasn't worked out so another step forward is required.

Four-time winner last season, 3 of those coming over C&D. Mixed record since scoring at Wolverhampton on return but she shaped better at Sandown latest and could be ready to strike back at this venue off a winning mark.
Won 3 times over 5f in 2025, including a better race than this on this card off 3 lb higher. However, he's proved most disappointing on turf this season.
Two 5f Chepstow wins on different ground this summer. Easy to forgive latest run at Chester and he's gone close a few times here before, including this season.
Ayr maiden winner in 2025 who was also an excellent sixth in Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot for John O'Donoghue. Well held all 5 starts this season for current yard, however. Headgear now applied.

Easily best effort in qualifying runs at 2 yrs when third at Salisbury on second start. That form looks much better now so one to note in the market on handicap bow after a year off (has been gelded).
Veteran who enhanced his good record at Windsor when third there 3 weeks ago, worth marking up given he came from much further back than the pair that beat him.
Winner here last season and was back to her best when successful off this mark at Lingfield (6f, turf) in June. However, recent efforts suggest she's gone off the boil.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap
races.verdict: DISTILLATION took his C&D form figures to 2121 when making all with ease last Monday and should be tough to beat under a 6 lb-penalty. Dark Mandate has made a positive start for new trainer Eve Johnson Houghton and is the obvious danger. Deadline is next on the list.

runners.note: Second C&D success when making all with ease 8 days ago. A 6 lb-penalty seems unlikely to stop him if showing up in similar form.
Placed twice in 7f handicaps at Lingfield and ran respectably when fifth of 13 over 1m at Kempton when last seen 12 weeks ago.
Lightly-raced maiden who comes here on the back of a good fifth of 9 in handicap at Yarmouth (6f, good) 30 days ago. In the mix off a 3 lb lower mark.
Second over 7f at Brighton in June but well held in 2 outings for new stable since.
6/1, very good second of 9 in handicap at Lingfield (7f, all-weather) 17 days ago. That was only his second outing for this yard and can likely open his account soon.

Fair maiden who hit the frame in maiden/handicap company on turf in Ireland. Runner-up on all-weather for this yard at the start of the year but below par in 2 turf outings back from a break last month.

Acclamation filly who failed to improve for a switch to handicap company when fifth of 6 at Leicester (1m, good to firm) in a first-time hood (discarded) 10 weeks ago. Still early days but need to see more.
Made all in a 7f Ffos Las class 6 event last month but didn't get close to backing that up when well held over 6f at Ripon on Saturday.
Came good in 7f Yarmouth classified race last month. Fair fifth in 6f Windsor handicap next time but well beaten back at Yarmouth since.
Maiden who started the season quite well but has been below par on last 3 starts. Has work to do.
Made her first real impact when fourth over 6f at Carlisle in June but has failed to back it up 3 times since.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: George Boughey's OXBRIDGE doesn't have a high standard to aim at on debut and gets the vote, with confidence in his chance increased should the betting vibes be strong. Urumita was a bit disappointing at Windsor but is sure to go well if bouncing back to the level of her Newbury debut.

runners.note: Has hinted at ability on both turf starts but not enough to think he can win a novice.
In good hands but well held in pair of sprint novices over 3 months apart.
Foaled January 29. 75,000 gns breeze-up 2-y-o with a US pedigree. The market should help guide to expectations.

Foaled February 19. 160,000 gns Blue Point colt. Half-brother to useful 5f winner Air Force One. Dam, 2-y-o 5f winner, half-sister to smart 6f/7f winner Donnerschlag. Likely type making debut in a very winnable race.
40/1, fourteenth of 15 in maiden at Newbury (6f, good to firm) on debut 11 days ago. More one for the longer term on that evidence.
Hasn't beaten a rival in 3 starts.
No more than minor promise in a pair of 5f outings on turf in July. Has had a breathing operation ahead of this first outing for 10 weeks.

Looked in need of the experience but made an encouraging start when fourth of 10 in maiden at Newbury (6f, firm) in August. Subsequent Windsor fifth was underwhelming but good shout if back to the debut form.

races.name: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
races.verdict: METHGAL advanced his form significantly when making all at Kempton last week and a 5-lb penalty may not be enough to prevent the follow up here. Rye and Cosmic Clarets head the list of dangers.

runners.note: Found improvement when winning 11-runner handicap at Kempton (6f) 6 days ago, kept up to work. Looks well-in under a 5-lb penalty and holds leading claims on tapeta debut.
Bath maiden winner (6f) last summer but been a mixed 2026 campaign and arrives on back of a poor Goodwood run. Others more convincing.
Found improvement when winning 8-runner handicap at Lingfield (6f) last month. Well below that level at Southwell since but can't be discounted here. Visor back on.
Enjoyed a fine run of form in 3-y-o handicaps in the first half of this year. Back on his latest winning mark after blowing the start at Lingfield last time and return of usual hood could help.
Belatedly off the mark when narrowly taking 11-runner handicap over C&D 28 days ago. 3 lb rise fair and has the assistance of Billy Loughnane.
Still looking for first success and was never going (bumped early on) in handicap at Leicester 21 days ago. Work to do on tapeta debut. Blinkers back on.
Finally off the mark at Nottingham in July and confirmed that improvement when following up at Newmarket (6f) 2 weeks later. Not at same level more recently but remains feasibly treated.
Fair maiden for Richard & Peter Fahey and ran up to best, on debut for new yard, when second of 10 in handicap over C&D 8 days ago. Can race off same mark here and holds solid claims.
Overcame a wide draw when narrowly recording a second C&D success of the season here earlier this month. Not disgraced in higher grade here since and can make presence felt again.
Successful twice on all-weather at Lingfield during early part of 2026 but well below par more recently.
Yet to score on Flat or over hurdles and recent efforts over the obstacles have offered little encouragement. Blinkers back on.

Kept busy and turned in best effort of 2026 for George Margarson when very good second of 6 in handicap at Lingfield (5f, AW) 43 days ago, clear of rest. Since joined new yard and must enter calculations.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On Instagram Handicap
races.verdict: D DAY MAJOR WINTER hasn't been with James Owen long and took another step back in the right direction when runner-up here a fortnight ago. He can land the spoils. Notable Charm and Echo Valley are also of interest.

runners.note: C&D winner who gained a deserved first win of 2026 in 4-runner Redcar handicap (2m) in July. Not quite in same form since but remains on a workable mark.
Lost his way for Gavin Cromwell and has offered little either over hurdles or on Flat since joining Ben Lund.
Offered little in a trio of starts here in 2022. Registered 3 victories at Les Landes since but hard to know what to expect here.
Posted best effort for new yard when good second of 9 in handicap at this course (1¾m, 6/1) 14 days ago. Can race off same mark here and holds solid claims.
Three-time hurdle winner but modest at best on the Flat and finished well beaten on return from long break at Chester earlier this month.
Well over 4 years since his last success and it's hard to see him making much of an impact from just out of the weights.
Bumper winner for Rebecca Menzies but well beaten in 3 attempts on the Flat. Likely best watched on handicap debut.
Back from 3 months off when respectable fourth of 9 in handicap (22/1) at this course (1¾m) 14 days ago. Entitled to build on that and is 1 lb lower now.
Still looking for first success but found improvement when good second of 5 in handicap over C&D (28/1) 8 days ago and has been dropped 2 lb since. Player.
Has offered little in a handful of starts, including both outings for current yard at Leicester and Lingfield this summer. Takes a marked step up in distance now.
Ran near best when third of 4 in handicap at Newcastle (16.3f, 9/1) 24 days ago. Should give another good account but others preferred for win purposes. 1 lb out of the weights,

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: This can go to EQUION, who took advantage of a much-reduced mark when getting back to winning ways at Ffos Las last week and still look fairly treated, despite a 4-lb penalty. Kev and Tortola can also make their presence felt.

runners.note: C&D winner who bounced back to form when taking 9-runner handicap at Ffos Las (1m, soft, 5/2) 8 days ago, driven out. 4-lb penalty to carry now but must enter calculations.
Returned to winning ways over similar trip at Lingfield last month and posted respectable efforts on his next 2 starts. Needs to bounce back from a poor run at Windsor, though.
Yet to register a victory and he arrives out of sorts, only eighth of 13 in handicap at Southwell (1m, 33/1) 5 days ago. Best watched.
Off the mark on second start for this yard at Lingfield in August and backed that up with creditable second of 12 in handicap (11/2) at Bath (1¼m, good) 16 days ago. Shortlist material.
Capitalised on the drop into classified company for the first time at this course (7f) in June but not really built on that back in handicap company since. Figures off a handy mark, though.
Good second on final start for Charlie Johnston but changed hands without success a few times since (had breathing operation after last run). Cheekpieces quickly discarded.
Took a step back in right direction, on second start for new yard, when respectable fourth of 10 in handicap at this course (7f, 10/1) 8 days ago. Back up in trip. Warrants respect.
Long-standing maiden who arrives on back of respectable fifth of 14 in handicap at Bath (1m, good to firm) 17 days ago. Challenge is to build on that here.
Little impact in a handful of starts, running no sort of race at Ffos Las last week. Makes limited appeal.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: DUMFRIES has been cut plenty of slack by the handicapper and shaped much better than the bare result at Beverley last time. He makes plenty of appeal. Book Of Life and Nicely Curved may prove the chief threats.

runners.note: Remains a long a time without a win but made the frame again when fourth of 8 in handicap at Musselburgh (1m, good to firm) 17 days ago, nearest finish. Enters calculations.

Gained reward for a string of solid efforts when shedding maiden tag in classified race at Chepstow (1m) in July and posted fine second at Ffos Las 4 days later. Below that level since, however, and others look better tr
Below last winning mark and arrives on back of creditable third of 10 in handicap at Beverley over similar trip 13 days ago. One to consider.

Sole success came at Newcastle for Ben Brookhouse on debut in 2023. Back in good form of late though for new yard, most recently when creditable third of 11 in handicap at Lingfield (7f, AW) 19 days ago. One of likelier
Fourteen runs since last win in 2024 for Richard Hughes. Made the frame a couple of times at Les Landes more recently but it's hard to know the value of that form.

Made the frame all 4 starts this season, latest when creditable third of 10 in minor event at Yarmouth (1m, firm) 46 days ago. Cheekpieces now added for first time and ought to go well again on handicap/tapeta debut.

Struggles for consistency nowadays but scored in a classified event over C&D in March and ran to a similar level here on her penultimate start. Below par at Ffos Las since but better expected back at this venue with hood
Successful twice on all-weather earlier in the year but not been in same form more recently. Fairly treated if revived following a break. 1 lb out of the handicap.
Yet to trouble the judge after 8 attempts and is readily passed over. Cheekpieces on for first time.
